translation.english_text: (Paranthaman enters, removes his coat and hangs it on the stand, then goes upstairs. As he climbs, he throws away his cigarette; it falls into the pocket of the hanging coat. The pocket begins to smoke. Poomalai, passing that way, sees the coat catching fire, runs to it and puts it out. In the coat pocket she finds the bundle of notes received from the mill owner, sealed 'Sivasakthi Mills,' and her expression changes. In the same pocket is a small slip.)
notes: This single bracketed source direction crosses PDF 52→53 and is retained as one cross-page translation unit.

translation.english_text:
Kalyani ... 1000
Subathra ... 300
Sulochana ... 500
Devaki ... 1200
notes: The four-name amount list is printed on the slip found in Paranthaman's coat.

translation.english_text: (Poomalai takes these and goes inside. Pandiyan arrives holding a newspaper, comes into the hall, sits down and reads.)
SIVASAKTHI MILL STRIKE ENDED. WORKERS RETURNED TO WORK.
notes: Translated from the bold newspaper headline explicitly quoted in the scene.

translation.english_text: (Pandiyan reads the bold headline carefully. Paranthaman comes downstairs, looks at his coat and finds the money missing. He goes to Pandiyan, who is reading, and feels around Pandiyan's pocket searching for it.)
What are you looking for?
Money....
Ask me; I'll give you some....
(Pandiyan takes out a ten-rupee note and gives it to him.)
(Laughing mockingly) What a fine thief! Are you going to give me the money properly or not?...
What are you saying now?
Hey! So that's it. You've started stealing even inside the house! Even I don't steal at home.
(He hears a voice call 'Paranthama,' turns, and Poomalai enters.)
What is it?
Look, Akka. I had some money; he stole it.
Which money?
I brought it from the publishing office.
I know where you brought it from.
That's the truth, Akka!

Look, it has a seal on it. You thundered, 'For the toiling worker with a backbone, is Mukhari the enchanting song?' Look—the seal says this is money the mill owner gave you as a reward for that thunderous slogan!
notes: `முகாரி` is retained as Mukhari rather than replaced by an inferred emotional gloss.

translation.english_text: (She shows the bundle of money. The Sivasakthi Mill seal is clearly visible.)
Oh.... so he stole the money and gave it to you?
Enough! After acting as a blackleg, betraying the poor and taking a payoff, you still have the nerve to speak.
Akka! You don't know why I took it. It was to add it to the workers' welfare fund!
I read that too.... Look here. One thousand for Kalyani, three hundred for Subathra, five hundred for Sulochana, one thousand two hundred for Devaki.

(Trying to manage the situation) Ha ha ha—oh, oh, did you misunderstand that? Ayyo, Rama, Muruga! Garudan and I are going to open a cinema theatre. Kalyani, Subathra, Sulochana, Devaki—this is the account of advances paid to release all those films there! Ha ha ha, ayyo, ayyo.
(He picks up the money and the slip that Poomalai placed on the table. His mocking laughter turns to anger and, in the same action, he turns to Pandiyan.)
Hey, you're the cause of all this.
The cause of what? Of your taking a bribe, or of betraying the workers?
Speak respectfully!
(Kumudha comes in.)
You should learn that yourself, Uncle!
(She comes and stands beside Pandiyan. Realising the situation may worsen, Poomalai turns to Kumudha.)
Kumudha! Take him inside, dear!
(Pandiyan turns to go inside with Kumudha.)
Yes! Take him inside, sing 'Aararo,' and lull the baby to sleep!
(Angrily) Enough!
(Sharply) Kumudha!
(Kumudha leaves with Pandiyan.)
I can't tell whether this is a house or a brothel!
Paranthama! Speak calmly!
Then what? Is it proper to let an unmarried girl go around with some good-for-nothing fellow?
She is married. Pandiyan and Kumudha are husband and wife.
A Gandharva marriage—or did you dream it up?
A registered marriage.
A registered marriage. I am here—there is still a man in this house. A registered marriage without my knowing....
notes: Historical unit ID u049 is retained rather than renumbered during corrected-source reconciliation.

translation.english_text: You live in this house? At least the word 'house' has come from your mouth—that alone makes me happy!...
notes: Recovered explicitly labelled source utterance; new translation unit added without renumbering historical translation-unit IDs.

translation.english_text: Akka! I understand you now. I understand that all the affection you showed, calling me 'little brother, little brother,' was mere pretence. Otherwise, after telling me as though affection overflowed, 'Kumudha lives for you; she is your wife,' would you now say that you have made her the wife of some orphaned fellow!
notes: Recovered explicitly labelled source utterance; new translation unit added without renumbering historical translation-unit IDs.

translation.english_text: Why do you need a wife? Whenever you wish, wives are available to you! For those beauties who ask for wealth without asking for love, there are innocent workers to pawn to the mill owner so that you can lavish money on them...
notes: This labelled utterance crosses PDF 56→57 and remains one translation unit.
Corrected-source reconciliation replaces the historical mistranscription of `அன்பைக் கேட்- / காமல் ஐஸ்வரியத்தைக் கேட்கும்` while preserving the genuine physical page split.

translation.english_text: Enough, stop!
Intelligent! Pure! I expected praises like these to come to you. I never imagined words of blame like 'debauchee' and 'wrongdoer' would come instead.
(Paranthaman leaves. Poomalai stands there, distressed, watching him go.)
notes: This stage-direction unit receives a new ID because historical u049 was already an immutable dialogue-linked unit after preserving existing translation IDs during reconciliation.
